segments.tr: - **Taxa de capitalização (Cap rate)** — O retorno derivado do mercado que os investidores exigem, expresso como NOI dividido pelo preço.

segments.src: - **Reconciliation** — The appraiser's final judgment weighting the approaches into a single opinion of value.
segments.tr: - **Reconciliação** — O julgamento final do avaliador ponderando as abordagens em uma única opinião de valor.

segments.src: - **Appraisal gap** — The shortfall when a property appraises below the contract price, which the buyer must cover in cash.
segments.tr: - **Gap de avaliação** — O déficit quando uma propriedade é avaliada abaixo do preço do contrato, que o comprador deve cobrir em dinheiro.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B) Cost.** No comps and no income stream leaves only reconstruction cost less depreciation; this is the textbook special-purpose case.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **1 — (B) Custo.** Sem comparáveis e sem fluxo de renda, resta apenas o custo de reconstrução menos a depreciação; este é o caso clássico de finalidade especial.

segments.src: Note the leverage in that denominator: if the cap rate moved to 6%, the same income would be worth $1,000,000.
segments.tr: Observe a alavancagem nesse denominador: se a taxa de capitalização subisse para 6%, a mesma renda valeria $1.000.000.

segments.src: **3 — X (False).** Debt service is excluded from NOI.
segments.tr: **3 — F (Falso).** O serviço da dívida é excluído do NOI.

segments.src: NOI measures what the property earns; your loan terms describe how you bought it, and two buyers with different mortgages would otherwise arrive at different "values" for the identical building.*
segments.tr: O NOI mede o que a propriedade rende; os termos do seu empréstimo descrevem como você a comprou, e dois compradores com hipotecas diferentes chegariam, de outra forma, a "valores" diferentes para o mesmo prédio.*

in.title: [Real Estate 101 #10] Tiga Cara Menjawab Satu Pertanyaan: "Berapa Nilai Tempat Ini Sebenarnya?"

segments.src: > An appraiser doesn't guess at a number — they triangulate it three ways: what it would cost to rebuild, what similar properties just sold for, and how much income it throws off.
segments.tr: > Seorang penilai tidak menebak angka — mereka melakukan triangulasi dengan tiga cara: berapa biaya untuk membangun kembali, berapa harga jual properti serupa baru-baru ini, dan berapa banyak pendapatan yang dihasilkan properti tersebut.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: A price is what one buyer paid.
segments.tr: Harga adalah apa yang dibayar oleh satu pembeli.

segments.src: **Value** is what a typical, informed buyer *would* pay — and that's a harder question, because every parcel of land on earth is unique.
segments.tr: **Nilai** adalah apa yang *akan* dibayar oleh pembeli biasa yang terinformasi — dan itu adalah pertanyaan yang lebih sulit, karena setiap bidang tanah di bumi ini unik.

segments.src: You can't look up "3-bed ranch in Raleigh" on a stock ticker.
segments.tr: Anda tidak bisa mencari "rumah 3 kamar di Raleigh" di ticker saham.

segments.src: So the appraisal profession settled on three independent routes to the same answer.
segments.tr: Jadi, profesi penilai menetapkan tiga jalur independen menuju jawaban yang sama.

segments.src: Each one is a different question in disguise.
segments.tr: Masing-masing adalah pertanyaan berbeda yang disamarkan.

segments.src: The Cost Approach — "What would it cost to build this from scratch?"**
segments.tr: Pendekatan Biaya (Cost Approach) — "Berapa biaya untuk membangun ini dari nol?"**

segments.src: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value
segments.tr: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value

segments.src: You value the land as if vacant, add what it would cost today to build an equivalent structure (*replacement cost*), then subtract everything that has eaten away at that new-building value.
segments.tr: Anda menilai tanah seolah-olah kosong, menambahkan biaya yang diperlukan saat ini untuk membangun struktur yang setara (*biaya penggantian*), lalu mengurangi semua hal yang telah menggerogoti nilai bangunan baru tersebut.

segments.src: That last part, **accrued depreciation**, comes in three flavors:
segments.tr: Bagian terakhir itu, **penyusutan terakumulasi (accrued depreciation)**, memiliki tiga jenis:

segments.src: - *Physical deterioration* — the roof is 22 years old, the deck is soft.
segments.tr: - *Kerusakan fisik* — atap sudah berusia 22 tahun, dek sudah lapuk.

segments.src: - *Functional obsolescence* — a 4-bedroom house with one bathroom, or a 9-foot ceiling in a warehouse district that now wants 32 feet.
segments.tr: - *Keusangan fungsional* — rumah dengan 4 kamar tidur tetapi hanya satu kamar mandi, atau langit-langit setinggi 9 kaki di kawasan gudang yang sekarang membutuhkan 32 kaki.

segments.src: - *External obsolescence* — nothing is wrong with the building; they just approved a highway interchange 300 feet away. This one is off-site, so the owner can't fix it at any price.
segments.tr: - *Keusangan eksternal* — tidak ada yang salah dengan bangunannya; mereka baru saja menyetujui pembangunan simpang jalan raya 300 kaki jauhnya. Ini berada di luar lokasi, jadi pemilik tidak bisa memperbaikinya dengan harga berapa pun.

segments.src: The cost approach is strongest for brand-new construction (little depreciation to estimate) and for **special-purpose property** — a church, a fire station, a municipal water treatment plant.
segments.tr: Pendekatan biaya paling kuat untuk konstruksi baru (sedikit penyusutan untuk diestimasi) dan untuk **properti tujuan khusus** — gereja, pemadam kebakaran, instalasi pengolahan air kota.

segments.src: Nobody has "comparable sales" of fire stations, and a fire station doesn't collect rent.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang memiliki "penjualan sebanding" untuk pemadam kebakaran, dan pemadam kebakaran tidak menghasilkan sewa.

segments.src: It's also the approach behind your homeowner's insurance replacement coverage.
segments.tr: Ini juga merupakan pendekatan di balik cakupan penggantian asuransi pemilik rumah Anda.

segments.src: The Sales Comparison Approach — "What did the neighbors get?"**
segments.tr: Pendekatan Perbandingan Penjualan (Sales Comparison Approach) — "Berapa harga yang didapat tetangga?"**

segments.src: Find three to five recent sales of genuinely similar properties (**comps**), then adjust *the comps* toward the subject property.
segments.tr: Temukan tiga hingga lima penjualan properti yang benar-benar serupa baru-baru ini (**pembanding/comps**), lalu sesuaikan *pembanding tersebut* terhadap properti subjek.

segments.src: Note the direction, because it trips everyone up: if the comp is **better** than your subject (it has the finished basement, yours doesn't), you **subtract** from the comp's sale price.
segments.tr: Perhatikan arahnya, karena ini sering membingungkan semua orang: jika pembanding **lebih baik** daripada subjek Anda (memiliki ruang bawah tanah jadi, milik Anda tidak), Anda **mengurangi** dari harga jual pembanding.

segments.src: If the comp is worse, you add.
segments.tr: Jika pembanding lebih buruk, Anda menambahkannya.

segments.src: You never adjust the subject — the subject is the unknown you're solving for.
segments.tr: Anda tidak pernah menyesuaikan subjek — subjek adalah hal yang tidak diketahui yang sedang Anda cari nilainya.

segments.src: This is the dominant approach for houses, condos, and vacant land, and it's what a lender's appraisal on a single-family purchase leans on almost entirely.
segments.tr: Ini adalah pendekatan dominan untuk rumah, kondominium, dan tanah kosong, dan inilah yang hampir sepenuhnya diandalkan oleh penilaian pemberi pinjaman pada pembelian keluarga tunggal.

segments.src: Its weakness is its dependency: it needs an active market of recent, arm's-length sales.
segments.tr: Kelemahannya adalah ketergantungannya: ia membutuhkan pasar aktif dari penjualan terkini yang dilakukan secara wajar (arm's-length).

segments.src: In a thin rural market or a frozen one, there's nothing to compare against.
segments.tr: Di pasar pedesaan yang tipis atau pasar yang beku, tidak ada yang bisa dibandingkan.

segments.src: The Income Capitalization Approach — "What does this thing earn?"**
segments.tr: Pendekatan Kapitalisasi Pendapatan (Income Capitalization Approach) — "Apa yang dihasilkan benda ini?"**

segments.src: For property bought as an investment, value is a function of the income stream.
segments.tr: Untuk properti yang dibeli sebagai investasi, nilai adalah fungsi dari aliran pendapatan.

segments.src: The simplest form is **direct capitalization**:
segments.tr: Bentuk paling sederhana adalah **kapitalisasi langsung**:

segments.src: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate
segments.tr: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate

segments.src: **NOI** is annual rent minus vacancy and collection loss, minus operating expenses (taxes, insurance, management, maintenance).
segments.tr: **NOI** adalah sewa tahunan dikurangi kerugian kekosongan dan penagihan, dikurangi biaya operasional (pajak, asuransi, manajemen, pemeliharaan).

segments.src: Critically, NOI is calculated *before* the mortgage.
segments.tr: Secara kritis, NOI dihitung *sebelum* hipotek.

segments.src: Debt service is not an operating expense — it describes how *you* financed the deal, not what the building earns.
segments.tr: Pembayaran utang bukanlah biaya operasional — itu menggambarkan bagaimana *Anda* membiayai kesepakatan tersebut, bukan apa yang dihasilkan bangunan itu.

segments.src: Two buyers with different loans face the same NOI.
segments.tr: Dua pembeli dengan pinjaman berbeda menghadapi NOI yang sama.

segments.src: The **cap rate** is the market's required return, pulled from what comparable investment properties recently sold for.
segments.tr: **Tingkat kapitalisasi (cap rate)** adalah pengembalian yang diminta pasar, diambil dari harga jual properti investasi sebanding baru-baru ini.

segments.src: Lower cap rate = higher price per dollar of income = investors see it as safer or expect growth.
segments.tr: Cap rate lebih rendah = harga lebih tinggi per dolar pendapatan = investor melihatnya lebih aman atau mengharapkan pertumbuhan.

segments.src: For longer, lumpier income streams — a 12-year office lease with step-ups — appraisers use *yield capitalization*, discounting projected future cash flows back to present value (a DCF).
segments.tr: Untuk aliran pendapatan yang lebih panjang dan tidak teratur — sewa kantor 12 tahun dengan kenaikan bertahap — penilai menggunakan *kapitalisasi hasil (yield capitalization)*, mendiskon proyeksi arus kas masa depan kembali ke nilai sekarang (DCF).

segments.src: **Then comes reconciliation.** The appraiser develops whichever approaches are applicable and then **weights** them.
segments.tr: **Kemudian tibalah rekonsiliasi.** Penilai mengembangkan pendekatan mana pun yang berlaku dan kemudian **memberi bobot** pada pendekatan tersebut.

segments.src: This is not an average.
segments.tr: Ini bukan rata-rata.

segments.src: For a suburban house, sales comparison carries nearly all the weight.
segments.tr: Untuk rumah pinggiran kota, perbandingan penjualan membawa hampir semua bobot.

segments.src: For a new distribution center leased to a national tenant, income leads.
segments.tr: Untuk pusat distribusi baru yang disewakan kepada penyewa nasional, pendapatan yang memimpin.

segments.src: For that fire station, cost is basically all you have.
segments.tr: Untuk pemadam kebakaran itu, biaya pada dasarnya adalah semua yang Anda miliki.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: You're under contract on a house outside Charlotte, NC at **$420,000**.
segments.tr: Anda sedang dalam kontrak untuk sebuah rumah di luar Charlotte, NC seharga **$420.000**.

segments.src: You're putting 20% down and financing the rest.
segments.tr: Anda membayar uang muka 20% dan membiayai sisanya.

segments.src: Two weeks in, the lender's appraisal comes back at **$405,000**.
segments.tr: Dua minggu kemudian, penilaian pemberi pinjaman kembali di angka **$405.000**.

segments.src: Here's why that stings.
segments.tr: Inilah mengapa itu menyakitkan.

segments.src: A lender lends against the **lesser** of the purchase price or the appraised value.
segments.tr: Pemberi pinjaman meminjamkan berdasarkan nilai **terendah** antara harga pembelian atau nilai appraisal.

segments.src: At $420,000 you'd borrow $336,000 and bring $84,000.
segments.tr: Pada $420.000 Anda akan meminjam $336.000 dan membawa $84.000.

segments.src: At an appraised $405,000 the loan caps at $324,000 — so if the seller won't budge on price, you now need **$96,000** in cash.
segments.tr: Pada nilai appraisal $405.000, pinjaman dibatasi pada $324.000 — jadi jika penjual tidak mau menurunkan harga, Anda sekarang membutuhkan **$96.000** tunai.

segments.src: That $12,000 hole is the **appraisal gap**, and it's the single most common reason a residential deal renegotiates or dies.
segments.tr: Lubang $12.000 itu adalah **kesenjangan penilaian (appraisal gap)**, dan itu adalah alasan paling umum mengapa kesepakatan perumahan dinegosiasi ulang atau batal.

segments.src: The appraiser almost certainly got there through sales comparison: three nearby sales, adjusted for square footage, garage, lot, and condition.
segments.tr: Penilai hampir pasti sampai di sana melalui perbandingan penjualan: tiga penjualan terdekat, disesuaikan untuk luas bangunan, garasi, tanah, dan kondisi.

segments.src: Now walk to the end of that same street, where a rented 4-unit building is for sale.
segments.tr: Sekarang berjalanlah ke ujung jalan yang sama, di mana bangunan 4 unit yang disewakan sedang dijual.

segments.src: Nobody is pulling comps on square footage here.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang menarik data pembanding berdasarkan luas bangunan di sini.

segments.src: Gross rents run $72,000 a year; after 6% vacancy and roughly $19,700 in operating expenses, NOI is about **$48,000**.
segments.tr: Sewa kotor mencapai $72.000 setahun; setelah 6% kekosongan dan sekitar $19.700 biaya operasional, NOI adalah sekitar **$48.000**.

segments.src: Similar small multifamily in that submarket has been trading at a **6.5% cap rate**:
segments.tr: Multifamili kecil serupa di sub-pasar itu telah diperdagangkan pada **cap rate 6,5%**:

segments.src: Same street, same week, two completely different valuation logics — because one property is a place to live and the other is a machine that produces cash.
segments.tr: Jalan yang sama, minggu yang sama, dua logika penilaian yang sama sekali berbeda — karena satu properti adalah tempat tinggal dan yang lainnya adalah mesin yang menghasilkan uang.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Rekap 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. Cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization are three independent routes to one number, and the appraiser weights them rather than averaging them.
segments.tr: 1. Biaya, perbandingan penjualan, dan kapitalisasi pendapatan adalah tiga jalur independen menuju satu angka, dan penilai memberi bobot pada mereka alih-alih merata-ratakannya.

segments.src: 2. Sales comparison rules owner-occupied housing; income capitalization rules investment property; cost approach covers new construction, insurance, and special-purpose buildings with no market to compare against.
segments.tr: 2. Perbandingan penjualan menguasai perumahan yang ditempati pemilik; kapitalisasi pendapatan menguasai properti investasi; pendekatan biaya mencakup konstruksi baru, asuransi, dan bangunan tujuan khusus tanpa pasar untuk dibandingkan.

segments.src: 3. `Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` is the whole income approach in one line — and NOI is always calculated before your mortgage payment.
segments.tr: 3. `Nilai = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` adalah seluruh pendekatan pendapatan dalam satu baris — dan NOI selalu dihitung sebelum pembayaran hipotek Anda.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** A city is appraising a newly built public library.
segments.tr: **1.** Sebuah kota sedang menilai perpustakaan umum yang baru dibangun.

segments.src: There are no comparable sales and it generates no rent.
segments.tr: Tidak ada penjualan sebanding dan tidak menghasilkan sewa.

segments.src: Which approach carries the most weight?
segments.tr: Pendekatan mana yang memiliki bobot paling besar?

segments.src: - (A) Sales comparison
segments.tr: - (A) Perbandingan penjualan

segments.src: - (B) Cost
segments.tr: - (B) Biaya

segments.src: - (C) Income capitalization
segments.tr: - (C) Kapitalisasi pendapatan

segments.src: - (D) Gross rent multiplier
segments.tr: - (D) Pengali sewa kotor

segments.src: **2.** A small retail strip produces $60,000 in NOI.
segments.tr: **2.** Sebuah strip ritel kecil menghasilkan $60.000 NOI.

segments.src: Comparable properties are trading at a 5% cap rate.
segments.tr: Properti sebanding diperdagangkan pada cap rate 5%.

segments.src: Estimated value?
segments.tr: Estimasi nilai?

segments.src: **3.** (O/X) Your monthly mortgage payment is an operating expense and should be subtracted when calculating a property's NOI.
segments.tr: **3.** (O/X) Pembayaran hipotek bulanan Anda adalah biaya operasional dan harus dikurangi saat menghitung NOI properti.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Comparable ("comp")** — A recently sold, genuinely similar property used as evidence of the subject's value.
segments.tr: - **Pembanding ("comp")** — Properti yang baru saja terjual dan benar-benar serupa yang digunakan sebagai bukti nilai subjek.

segments.src: - **Accrued depreciation** — Total loss in value from all causes since construction: physical, functional, and external.
segments.tr: - **Penyusutan terakumulasi** — Total kehilangan nilai dari semua penyebab sejak konstruksi: fisik, fungsional, dan eksternal.

segments.src: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** — Income after vacancy and operating expenses, but *before* debt service and income taxes.
segments.tr: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** — Pendapatan setelah kekosongan dan biaya operasional, tetapi *sebelum* pembayaran utang dan pajak penghasilan.

segments.src: - **Capitalization rate** — The market-derived return investors demand, expressed as NOI divided by price.
segments.tr: - **Tingkat kapitalisasi (Capitalization rate)** — Pengembalian yang dituntut investor yang berasal dari pasar, dinyatakan sebagai NOI dibagi dengan harga.

segments.src: - **Reconciliation** — The appraiser's final judgment weighting the approaches into a single opinion of value.
segments.tr: - **Rekonsiliasi** — Penilaian akhir penilai yang memberi bobot pada pendekatan-pendekatan menjadi satu opini nilai tunggal.

segments.src: - **Appraisal gap** — The shortfall when a property appraises below the contract price, which the buyer must cover in cash.
segments.tr: - **Kesenjangan penilaian (Appraisal gap)** — Kekurangan saat properti dinilai di bawah harga kontrak, yang harus ditutupi pembeli secara tunai.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B) Cost.** No comps and no income stream leaves only reconstruction cost less depreciation; this is the textbook special-purpose case.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1 — (B) Biaya.** Tidak ada pembanding dan tidak ada aliran pendapatan menyisakan hanya biaya rekonstruksi dikurangi penyusutan; ini adalah kasus tujuan khusus dalam buku teks.

segments.src: Note the leverage in that denominator: if the cap rate moved to 6%, the same income would be worth $1,000,000.
segments.tr: Perhatikan leverage pada penyebut tersebut: jika cap rate bergerak ke 6%, pendapatan yang sama akan bernilai $1.000.000.

segments.src: **3 — X (False).** Debt service is excluded from NOI.
segments.tr: **3 — X (Salah).** Pembayaran utang dikecualikan dari NOI.

segments.src: NOI measures what the property earns; your loan terms describe how you bought it, and two buyers with different mortgages would otherwise arrive at different "values" for the identical building.*
segments.tr: NOI mengukur apa yang dihasilkan properti; ketentuan pinjaman Anda menggambarkan bagaimana Anda membelinya, dan dua pembeli dengan hipotek berbeda akan menghasilkan "nilai" yang berbeda untuk bangunan yang identik.*

ja.title: [不動産101 #10] 1つの問いに対する3つの答え：「この物件の本当の価値はいくらか？」

segments.src: > An appraiser doesn't guess at a number — they triangulate it three ways: what it would cost to rebuild, what similar properties just sold for, and how much income it throws off.
segments.tr: > 不動産鑑定士は数値を推測するのではなく、3つの方法で算出します。再建築にかかる費用、類似物件の直近の売却価格、そしてその物件が生み出す収益です。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: A price is what one buyer paid.
segments.tr: 価格とは、ある買い手が支払った金額のことです。

segments.src: **Value** is what a typical, informed buyer *would* pay — and that's a harder question, because every parcel of land on earth is unique.
segments.tr: **価値**とは、情報に通じた一般的な買い手が支払うであろう金額のことです。地球上のすべての土地は唯一無二であるため、これはより難しい問いとなります。

segments.src: You can't look up "3-bed ranch in Raleigh" on a stock ticker.
segments.tr: 株式相場のように「ローリーの3ベッドルームのランチハウス」を検索することはできません。

segments.src: So the appraisal profession settled on three independent routes to the same answer.
segments.tr: そこで鑑定業界は、同じ答えにたどり着くための3つの独立したルートを確立しました。

segments.src: Each one is a different question in disguise.
segments.tr: それぞれが、形を変えた異なる問いかけになっています。

segments.src: The Cost Approach — "What would it cost to build this from scratch?"**
segments.tr: 原価法（コストアプローチ） — 「ゼロからこれを建てるのにいくらかかるか？」**

segments.src: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value
segments.tr: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value

segments.src: You value the land as if vacant, add what it would cost today to build an equivalent structure (*replacement cost*), then subtract everything that has eaten away at that new-building value.
segments.tr: 土地を更地と仮定して評価し、同等の建物を今日建てるのにかかる費用（*再調達原価*）を加え、新築時の価値を損なわせているすべての要因を差し引きます。

segments.src: That last part, **accrued depreciation**, comes in three flavors:
segments.tr: 最後の部分である**累積減価**には、3つの種類があります：

segments.src: - *Physical deterioration* — the roof is 22 years old, the deck is soft.
segments.tr: - *物理的劣化* — 屋根が築22年、デッキが傷んでいるなど。

segments.src: - *Functional obsolescence* — a 4-bedroom house with one bathroom, or a 9-foot ceiling in a warehouse district that now wants 32 feet.
segments.tr: - *機能的減価* — 4ベッドルームの家なのにバスルームが1つしかない、あるいは32フィートの天井高が求められる倉庫街で天井が9フィートしかないなど。

segments.src: - *External obsolescence* — nothing is wrong with the building; they just approved a highway interchange 300 feet away. This one is off-site, so the owner can't fix it at any price.
segments.tr: - *経済的減価* — 建物自体に問題はないが、300フィート先に高速道路のインターチェンジが承認された場合など。これは敷地外の要因であるため、所有者はどんなにお金を払っても解決できません。

segments.src: The cost approach is strongest for brand-new construction (little depreciation to estimate) and for **special-purpose property** — a church, a fire station, a municipal water treatment plant.
segments.tr: 原価法は、新築物件（推定すべき減価が少ない）や、教会、消防署、自治体の浄水場といった**特殊目的物件**に最も適しています。

segments.src: Nobody has "comparable sales" of fire stations, and a fire station doesn't collect rent.
segments.tr: 消防署の「比較可能な売却事例」など存在しませんし、消防署は賃料を徴収しません。

segments.src: It's also the approach behind your homeowner's insurance replacement coverage.
segments.tr: また、これは住宅所有者の火災保険における再調達価額補償の根拠となる手法でもあります。

segments.src: The Sales Comparison Approach — "What did the neighbors get?"**
segments.tr: 取引事例比較法（セールス・コンパリゾン・アプローチ） — 「近隣ではいくらで売れたか？」**

segments.src: Find three to five recent sales of genuinely similar properties (**comps**), then adjust *the comps* toward the subject property.
segments.tr: 真に類似した物件（**比較物件**）の直近の売却事例を3〜5件見つけ、その*比較物件*を対象物件に合わせて調整します。

segments.src: Note the direction, because it trips everyone up: if the comp is **better** than your subject (it has the finished basement, yours doesn't), you **subtract** from the comp's sale price.
segments.tr: 調整の方向に注意してください。誰もがここでつまずきます。比較物件が対象物件より**優れている**場合（完成済みの地下室があるなど）、比較物件の売却価格から**差し引きます**。

segments.src: If the comp is worse, you add.
segments.tr: 比較物件の方が劣っている場合は、加算します。

segments.src: You never adjust the subject — the subject is the unknown you're solving for.
segments.tr: 対象物件を調整してはいけません。対象物件こそが、あなたが解こうとしている未知の変数だからです。

segments.src: This is the dominant approach for houses, condos, and vacant land, and it's what a lender's appraisal on a single-family purchase leans on almost entirely.
segments.tr: これは住宅、コンドミニアム、更地において支配的な手法であり、一戸建て購入時の融資機関による鑑定のほとんどがこれに依存しています。

segments.src: Its weakness is its dependency: it needs an active market of recent, arm's-length sales.
segments.tr: この手法の弱点は依存性にあります。直近の、第三者間での活発な市場取引が必要です。

segments.src: In a thin rural market or a frozen one, there's nothing to compare against.
segments.tr: 市場が停滞している地方や、取引が凍結している市場では、比較対象が何もありません。

segments.src: The Income Capitalization Approach — "What does this thing earn?"**
segments.tr: 収益還元法（インカム・キャピタリゼーション・アプローチ） — 「この物件はいくら稼ぐか？」**

segments.src: For property bought as an investment, value is a function of the income stream.
segments.tr: 投資目的で購入される物件にとって、価値とは収益の流れの関数です。

segments.src: The simplest form is **direct capitalization**:
segments.tr: 最も単純な形式は**直接還元法**です：

segments.src: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate
segments.tr: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate

segments.src: **NOI** is annual rent minus vacancy and collection loss, minus operating expenses (taxes, insurance, management, maintenance).
segments.tr: **NOI（純営業利益）**は、年間賃料から空室損や回収不能損、運営経費（税金、保険、管理費、修繕費）を差し引いたものです。

segments.src: Critically, NOI is calculated *before* the mortgage.
segments.tr: 重要な点として、NOIは住宅ローン返済額を差し引く*前*に計算されます。

segments.src: Debt service is not an operating expense — it describes how *you* financed the deal, not what the building earns.
segments.tr: 負債サービス（ローン返済）は運営経費ではありません。それは*あなた*がどのように取引に融資したかを示すものであり、建物が稼ぐ金額とは無関係です。

segments.src: Two buyers with different loans face the same NOI.
segments.tr: 異なるローンを組んだ2人の買い手であっても、NOIは同じです。

segments.src: The **cap rate** is the market's required return, pulled from what comparable investment properties recently sold for.
segments.tr: **還元利回り（キャップレート）**は、市場が要求する収益率であり、類似の投資物件が最近いくらで売却されたかから導き出されます。

segments.src: Lower cap rate = higher price per dollar of income = investors see it as safer or expect growth.
segments.tr: キャップレートが低いほど、収益1ドルあたりの価格は高くなります。これは投資家がその物件をより安全だと見なしているか、成長を期待していることを意味します。

segments.src: For longer, lumpier income streams — a 12-year office lease with step-ups — appraisers use *yield capitalization*, discounting projected future cash flows back to present value (a DCF).
segments.tr: 12年間のオフィス賃貸契約で段階的に賃料が上がるような、より長く複雑な収益の流れに対しては、鑑定士は*DCF法（収益還元法の一種）*を用い、将来の予測キャッシュフローを現在価値に割り引きます。

segments.src: **Then comes reconciliation.** The appraiser develops whichever approaches are applicable and then **weights** them.
segments.tr: **そして、最後に調整（Reconciliation）を行います。** 鑑定士は適用可能な手法を展開し、それらに**重み付け**を行います。

segments.src: This is not an average.
segments.tr: これは単なる平均ではありません。

segments.src: For a suburban house, sales comparison carries nearly all the weight.
segments.tr: 郊外の住宅であれば、取引事例比較法がほぼすべての重みを占めます。

segments.src: For a new distribution center leased to a national tenant, income leads.
segments.tr: 全国的なテナントに賃貸されている新しい物流センターであれば、収益還元法が主導します。

segments.src: For that fire station, cost is basically all you have.
segments.tr: あの消防署のような物件であれば、原価法がほぼすべてとなります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活における例

segments.src: You're under contract on a house outside Charlotte, NC at **$420,000**.
segments.tr: あなたはノースカロライナ州シャーロット郊外の住宅を**42万ドル**で契約しました。

segments.src: You're putting 20% down and financing the rest.
segments.tr: 頭金を20%支払い、残りを融資で賄う予定です。

segments.src: Two weeks in, the lender's appraisal comes back at **$405,000**.
segments.tr: 2週間後、融資機関の鑑定結果が**40万5,000ドル**で返ってきました。

segments.src: Here's why that stings.
segments.tr: なぜこれが痛手なのか。

segments.src: A lender lends against the **lesser** of the purchase price or the appraised value.
segments.tr: 融資機関は、購入価格と鑑定評価額の**いずれか低い方**を基準に融資を行うからです。

segments.src: At $420,000 you'd borrow $336,000 and bring $84,000.
segments.tr: 42万ドルであれば33万6,000ドルを借り入れ、8万4,000ドルを用意すれば済みます。

segments.src: At an appraised $405,000 the loan caps at $324,000 — so if the seller won't budge on price, you now need **$96,000** in cash.
segments.tr: しかし鑑定額が40万5,000ドルだと、融資上限は32万4,000ドルになります。そのため、売り手が価格を譲歩しなければ、あなたは**9万6,000ドル**の現金を準備する必要があります。

segments.src: That $12,000 hole is the **appraisal gap**, and it's the single most common reason a residential deal renegotiates or dies.
segments.tr: この1万2,000ドルの穴は**鑑定ギャップ**と呼ばれ、住宅取引が再交渉になったり破談になったりする最も一般的な理由です。

segments.src: The appraiser almost certainly got there through sales comparison: three nearby sales, adjusted for square footage, garage, lot, and condition.
segments.tr: 鑑定士はほぼ間違いなく、取引事例比較法を用いてこの結論に至りました。近隣の3件の売却事例を、床面積、ガレージ、敷地、状態に基づいて調整した結果です。

segments.src: Now walk to the end of that same street, where a rented 4-unit building is for sale.
segments.tr: 次に、同じ通りの突き当たりにある、賃貸中の4戸建てビルが売りに出されているとします。

segments.src: Nobody is pulling comps on square footage here.
segments.tr: ここでは誰も床面積で比較事例（コンプ）を拾ったりしません。

segments.src: Gross rents run $72,000 a year; after 6% vacancy and roughly $19,700 in operating expenses, NOI is about **$48,000**.
segments.tr: 総賃料収入は年間7万2,000ドル。6%の空室損と約1万9,700ドルの運営経費を差し引くと、NOIは約**4万8,000ドル**です。

segments.src: Similar small multifamily in that submarket has been trading at a **6.5% cap rate**:
segments.tr: そのサブマーケットの同様の小規模集合住宅は、**6.5%のキャップレート**で取引されています：

segments.src: Same street, same week, two completely different valuation logics — because one property is a place to live and the other is a machine that produces cash.
segments.tr: 同じ通り、同じ週であっても、評価ロジックは全く異なります。なぜなら、一方は住む場所であり、もう一方は現金を産み出す機械だからです。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization are three independent routes to one number, and the appraiser weights them rather than averaging them.
segments.tr: 1. 原価法、取引事例比較法、収益還元法は、1つの数値にたどり着くための3つの独立したルートであり、鑑定士はそれらを平均するのではなく重み付けを行います。

segments.src: 2. Sales comparison rules owner-occupied housing; income capitalization rules investment property; cost approach covers new construction, insurance, and special-purpose buildings with no market to compare against.
segments.tr: 2. 取引事例比較法は居住用住宅を支配し、収益還元法は投資物件を支配し、原価法は新築、保険、比較対象のない特殊目的物件をカバーします。

segments.src: 3. `Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` is the whole income approach in one line — and NOI is always calculated before your mortgage payment.
segments.tr: 3. `価値 = NOI ÷ キャップレート` が収益還元法のすべてを1行で表したものです。そしてNOIは常に住宅ローン返済額を差し引く前に計算されます。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ セルフクイズ

segments.src: **1.** A city is appraising a newly built public library.
segments.tr: **1.** 市が新築の公共図書館を鑑定しています。

segments.src: There are no comparable sales and it generates no rent.
segments.tr: 比較可能な売却事例はなく、賃料も発生しません。

segments.src: Which approach carries the most weight?
segments.tr: どの手法が最も重みを持つでしょうか？

segments.src: - (A) Sales comparison
segments.tr: - (A) 取引事例比較法

segments.src: - (B) Cost
segments.tr: - (B) 原価法

segments.src: - (C) Income capitalization
segments.tr: - (C) 収益還元法

segments.src: - (D) Gross rent multiplier
segments.tr: - (D) 総収益乗数法

segments.src: **2.** A small retail strip produces $60,000 in NOI.
segments.tr: **2.** 小規模な小売店舗が6万ドルのNOIを生み出しています。

segments.src: Comparable properties are trading at a 5% cap rate.
segments.tr: 類似物件は5%のキャップレートで取引されています。

segments.src: Estimated value?
segments.tr: 推定価値は？
- (A) 30万ドル
- (B) 120万ドル
- (C) 300万ドル

segments.src: **3.** (O/X) Your monthly mortgage payment is an operating expense and should be subtracted when calculating a property's NOI.
segments.tr: **3.** (○/×) 毎月の住宅ローン返済額は運営経費であり、物件のNOIを計算する際に差し引くべきである。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Comparable ("comp")** — A recently sold, genuinely similar property used as evidence of the subject's value.
segments.tr: - **比較物件（コンプ）** — 対象物件の価値の証拠として使用される、最近売却された真に類似した物件。

segments.src: - **Accrued depreciation** — Total loss in value from all causes since construction: physical, functional, and external.
segments.tr: - **累積減価** — 建設以来、物理的、機能的、経済的など、あらゆる原因によって生じた価値の総損失。

segments.src: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** — Income after vacancy and operating expenses, but *before* debt service and income taxes.
segments.tr: - **純営業利益（NOI）** — 空室損や運営経費を差し引いた後の利益。ただし、負債サービス（ローン返済）や所得税を差し引く*前*のもの。

segments.src: - **Capitalization rate** — The market-derived return investors demand, expressed as NOI divided by price.
segments.tr: - **還元利回り（キャップレート）** — 投資家が要求する市場から導き出される収益率。NOIを価格で割ったもの。

segments.src: - **Reconciliation** — The appraiser's final judgment weighting the approaches into a single opinion of value.
segments.tr: - **調整（Reconciliation）** — 鑑定士が各手法を重み付けし、最終的な価値判断を下すこと。

segments.src: - **Appraisal gap** — The shortfall when a property appraises below the contract price, which the buyer must cover in cash.
segments.tr: - **鑑定ギャップ** — 物件の鑑定額が契約価格を下回った際に生じる不足分。買い手が現金で補填しなければならない。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B) Cost.** No comps and no income stream leaves only reconstruction cost less depreciation; this is the textbook special-purpose case.
segments.tr: *回答: **1 — (B) 原価法。** 比較事例も収益の流れもない場合、残るのは減価を差し引いた再建築原価のみです。これは特殊目的物件の典型的なケースです。

segments.src: Note the leverage in that denominator: if the cap rate moved to 6%, the same income would be worth $1,000,000.
segments.tr: 分母のレバレッジに注目してください。もしキャップレートが6%に動けば、同じ収益でも価値は100万ドルになります。

segments.src: **3 — X (False).** Debt service is excluded from NOI.
segments.tr: **3 — × (誤り)。** 負債サービスはNOIから除外されます。

segments.src: NOI measures what the property earns; your loan terms describe how you bought it, and two buyers with different mortgages would otherwise arrive at different "values" for the identical building.*
segments.tr: NOIは物件が稼ぐ金額を測定するものであり、ローン条件はあなたがそれをどう購入したかを示すものです。もしローン条件を含めてしまうと、同じ建物であっても、異なるローンを組んだ2人の買い手によって異なる「価値」が算出されてしまうことになります。*

de.title: [Immobilien 101 #10] Drei Wege, eine Frage zu beantworten: „Was ist dieser Ort eigentlich wert?“

segments.src: > An appraiser doesn't guess at a number — they triangulate it three ways: what it would cost to rebuild, what similar properties just sold for, and how much income it throws off.
segments.tr: > Ein Gutachter rät nicht einfach eine Zahl – er trianguliert sie auf drei Wegen: was ein Wiederaufbau kosten würde, was ähnliche Immobilien gerade erzielt haben und wie viel Einkommen sie abwirft.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: A price is what one buyer paid.
segments.tr: Ein Preis ist das, was ein Käufer bezahlt hat.

segments.src: **Value** is what a typical, informed buyer *would* pay — and that's a harder question, because every parcel of land on earth is unique.
segments.tr: **Wert** ist das, was ein typischer, informierter Käufer zahlen *würde* – und das ist eine schwierigere Frage, denn jedes Grundstück auf der Welt ist einzigartig.

segments.src: You can't look up "3-bed ranch in Raleigh" on a stock ticker.
segments.tr: Man kann nicht einfach „3-Zimmer-Ranch in Raleigh“ auf einem Börsenticker nachschlagen.

segments.src: So the appraisal profession settled on three independent routes to the same answer.
segments.tr: Also hat sich das Gutachterwesen auf drei unabhängige Wege zur gleichen Antwort geeinigt.

segments.src: Each one is a different question in disguise.
segments.tr: Jeder davon ist eine andere Frage in Verkleidung.

segments.src: The Cost Approach — "What would it cost to build this from scratch?"**
segments.tr: Das Sachwertverfahren – „Was würde es kosten, das von Grund auf neu zu bauen?“**

segments.src: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value
segments.tr: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value

segments.src: You value the land as if vacant, add what it would cost today to build an equivalent structure (*replacement cost*), then subtract everything that has eaten away at that new-building value.
segments.tr: Man bewertet das Grundstück, als wäre es unbebaut, addiert die Kosten, die heute für den Bau einer gleichwertigen Struktur anfallen würden (*Wiederbeschaffungskosten*), und zieht dann alles ab, was den Wert des neuen Gebäudes gemindert hat.

segments.src: That last part, **accrued depreciation**, comes in three flavors:
segments.tr: Dieser letzte Teil, die **kumulierte Abschreibung**, kommt in drei Varianten:

segments.src: - *Physical deterioration* — the roof is 22 years old, the deck is soft.
segments.tr: - *Physischer Verfall* – das Dach ist 22 Jahre alt, die Terrasse ist morsch.

segments.src: - *Functional obsolescence* — a 4-bedroom house with one bathroom, or a 9-foot ceiling in a warehouse district that now wants 32 feet.
segments.tr: - *Funktionale Veralterung* – ein Haus mit 4 Schlafzimmern und nur einem Badezimmer oder eine 2,70 Meter hohe Decke in einem Lagerhausviertel, das heute 10 Meter verlangt.

segments.src: - *External obsolescence* — nothing is wrong with the building; they just approved a highway interchange 300 feet away. This one is off-site, so the owner can't fix it at any price.
segments.tr: - *Externe Veralterung* – mit dem Gebäude ist alles in Ordnung; es wurde nur ein Autobahnkreuz in 100 Metern Entfernung genehmigt. Dies liegt außerhalb des Grundstücks, daher kann der Eigentümer es zu keinem Preis beheben.

segments.src: The cost approach is strongest for brand-new construction (little depreciation to estimate) and for **special-purpose property** — a church, a fire station, a municipal water treatment plant.
segments.tr: Das Sachwertverfahren ist am stärksten bei Neubauten (wenig Abschreibung zu schätzen) und bei **Spezialimmobilien** – einer Kirche, einer Feuerwache, einem kommunalen Wasserwerk.

segments.src: Nobody has "comparable sales" of fire stations, and a fire station doesn't collect rent.
segments.tr: Niemand hat „vergleichbare Verkäufe“ von Feuerwachen, und eine Feuerwache erzielt keine Mieteinnahmen.

segments.src: It's also the approach behind your homeowner's insurance replacement coverage.
segments.tr: Es ist auch der Ansatz, der hinter der Wiederaufbauversicherung Ihres Eigenheims steht.

segments.src: The Sales Comparison Approach — "What did the neighbors get?"**
segments.tr: Das Vergleichswertverfahren – „Was haben die Nachbarn bekommen?“**

segments.src: Find three to five recent sales of genuinely similar properties (**comps**), then adjust *the comps* toward the subject property.
segments.tr: Finden Sie drei bis fünf kürzliche Verkäufe von wirklich ähnlichen Immobilien (**Vergleichsobjekte**), und passen Sie dann *die Vergleichsobjekte* an das Bewertungsobjekt an.

segments.src: Note the direction, because it trips everyone up: if the comp is **better** than your subject (it has the finished basement, yours doesn't), you **subtract** from the comp's sale price.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie die Richtung, denn da stolpern alle drüber: Wenn das Vergleichsobjekt **besser** ist als Ihr Bewertungsobjekt (es hat den ausgebauten Keller, Ihres nicht), **ziehen** Sie etwas vom Verkaufspreis des Vergleichsobjekts ab.

segments.src: If the comp is worse, you add.
segments.tr: Wenn das Vergleichsobjekt schlechter ist, addieren Sie etwas.

segments.src: You never adjust the subject — the subject is the unknown you're solving for.
segments.tr: Sie passen niemals das Bewertungsobjekt an – das Bewertungsobjekt ist die Unbekannte, die Sie lösen wollen.

segments.src: This is the dominant approach for houses, condos, and vacant land, and it's what a lender's appraisal on a single-family purchase leans on almost entirely.
segments.tr: Dies ist der dominierende Ansatz für Häuser, Eigentumswohnungen und unbebaute Grundstücke, und darauf stützt sich die Wertermittlung eines Kreditgebers beim Kauf eines Einfamilienhauses fast vollständig.

segments.src: Its weakness is its dependency: it needs an active market of recent, arm's-length sales.
segments.tr: Seine Schwäche ist seine Abhängigkeit: Er benötigt einen aktiven Markt mit kürzlichen, marktüblichen Verkäufen.

segments.src: In a thin rural market or a frozen one, there's nothing to compare against.
segments.tr: In einem dünnen ländlichen Markt oder einem eingefrorenen Markt gibt es nichts, womit man vergleichen könnte.

segments.src: The Income Capitalization Approach — "What does this thing earn?"**
segments.tr: Das Ertragswertverfahren – „Was verdient dieses Ding?“**

segments.src: For property bought as an investment, value is a function of the income stream.
segments.tr: Bei Immobilien, die als Investition gekauft werden, ist der Wert eine Funktion des Einkommensstroms.

segments.src: The simplest form is **direct capitalization**:
segments.tr: Die einfachste Form ist die **direkte Kapitalisierung**:

segments.src: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate
segments.tr: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate

segments.src: **NOI** is annual rent minus vacancy and collection loss, minus operating expenses (taxes, insurance, management, maintenance).
segments.tr: **NOI** (Netto-Betriebsergebnis) ist die Jahresmiete abzüglich Leerstand und Mietausfall sowie abzüglich der Betriebskosten (Steuern, Versicherung, Verwaltung, Instandhaltung).

segments.src: Critically, NOI is calculated *before* the mortgage.
segments.tr: Wichtig: Das NOI wird *vor* der Hypothek berechnet.

segments.src: Debt service is not an operating expense — it describes how *you* financed the deal, not what the building earns.
segments.tr: Der Schuldendienst ist keine Betriebskosten – er beschreibt, wie *Sie* das Geschäft finanziert haben, nicht, was das Gebäude verdient.

segments.src: Two buyers with different loans face the same NOI.
segments.tr: Zwei Käufer mit unterschiedlichen Krediten stehen vor demselben NOI.

segments.src: The **cap rate** is the market's required return, pulled from what comparable investment properties recently sold for.
segments.tr: Der **Kapitalisierungssatz** (Cap Rate) ist die vom Markt geforderte Rendite, abgeleitet von dem, was vergleichbare Anlageimmobilien kürzlich erzielt haben.

segments.src: Lower cap rate = higher price per dollar of income = investors see it as safer or expect growth.
segments.tr: Niedrigerer Kapitalisierungssatz = höherer Preis pro Dollar Einkommen = Investoren sehen es als sicherer an oder erwarten Wachstum.

segments.src: For longer, lumpier income streams — a 12-year office lease with step-ups — appraisers use *yield capitalization*, discounting projected future cash flows back to present value (a DCF).
segments.tr: Für längere, unregelmäßigere Einkommensströme – einen 12-jährigen Büro-Mietvertrag mit Staffelmieten – verwenden Gutachter die *Ertragskapitalisierung* (Yield Capitalization), bei der prognostizierte zukünftige Cashflows auf den Barwert abgezinst werden (eine DCF-Analyse).

segments.src: **Then comes reconciliation.** The appraiser develops whichever approaches are applicable and then **weights** them.
segments.tr: **Dann kommt die Abstimmung (Reconciliation).** Der Gutachter entwickelt die jeweils anwendbaren Ansätze und **gewichtet** sie dann.

segments.src: This is not an average.
segments.tr: Dies ist kein Durchschnitt.

segments.src: For a suburban house, sales comparison carries nearly all the weight.
segments.tr: Bei einem Vorstadthaus trägt das Vergleichswertverfahren fast das gesamte Gewicht.

segments.src: For a new distribution center leased to a national tenant, income leads.
segments.tr: Bei einem neuen Logistikzentrum, das an einen nationalen Mieter vermietet ist, führt der Ertragswert.

segments.src: For that fire station, cost is basically all you have.
segments.tr: Für diese Feuerwache ist der Sachwert im Grunde alles, was Sie haben.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: You're under contract on a house outside Charlotte, NC at **$420,000**.
segments.tr: Sie haben einen Vertrag für ein Haus außerhalb von Charlotte, NC für **$420.000**.

segments.src: You're putting 20% down and financing the rest.
segments.tr: Sie zahlen 20 % an und finanzieren den Rest.

segments.src: Two weeks in, the lender's appraisal comes back at **$405,000**.
segments.tr: Zwei Wochen später kommt die Wertermittlung des Kreditgebers bei **$405.000** zurück.

segments.src: Here's why that stings.
segments.tr: Hier ist der Grund, warum das schmerzt.

segments.src: A lender lends against the **lesser** of the purchase price or the appraised value.
segments.tr: Ein Kreditgeber verleiht Geld basierend auf dem **Niedrigeren** von Kaufpreis oder Schätzwert.

segments.src: At $420,000 you'd borrow $336,000 and bring $84,000.
segments.tr: Bei $420.000 würden Sie $336.000 leihen und $84.000 mitbringen.

segments.src: At an appraised $405,000 the loan caps at $324,000 — so if the seller won't budge on price, you now need **$96,000** in cash.
segments.tr: Bei einem geschätzten Wert von $405.000 ist das Darlehen auf $324.000 begrenzt – wenn der Verkäufer also beim Preis nicht nachgibt, benötigen Sie jetzt **$96.000** in bar.

segments.src: That $12,000 hole is the **appraisal gap**, and it's the single most common reason a residential deal renegotiates or dies.
segments.tr: Dieses $12.000-Loch ist die **Bewertungslücke** (Appraisal Gap), und es ist der häufigste Grund, warum ein Immobiliengeschäft neu verhandelt wird oder scheitert.

segments.src: The appraiser almost certainly got there through sales comparison: three nearby sales, adjusted for square footage, garage, lot, and condition.
segments.tr: Der Gutachter kam fast sicher durch das Vergleichswertverfahren dorthin: drei nahegelegene Verkäufe, angepasst an Quadratmeterzahl, Garage, Grundstück und Zustand.

segments.src: Now walk to the end of that same street, where a rented 4-unit building is for sale.
segments.tr: Gehen Sie nun zum Ende derselben Straße, wo ein vermietetes 4-Parteien-Haus zum Verkauf steht.

segments.src: Nobody is pulling comps on square footage here.
segments.tr: Niemand zieht hier Vergleichswerte basierend auf Quadratmetern heran.

segments.src: Gross rents run $72,000 a year; after 6% vacancy and roughly $19,700 in operating expenses, NOI is about **$48,000**.
segments.tr: Die Bruttomieten betragen $72.000 pro Jahr; nach 6 % Leerstand und etwa $19.700 an Betriebskosten beträgt das NOI etwa **$48.000**.

segments.src: Similar small multifamily in that submarket has been trading at a **6.5% cap rate**:
segments.tr: Ähnliche kleine Mehrfamilienhäuser in diesem Teilmarkt werden mit einer **6,5 % Cap Rate** gehandelt:

segments.src: Same street, same week, two completely different valuation logics — because one property is a place to live and the other is a machine that produces cash.
segments.tr: Dieselbe Straße, dieselbe Woche, zwei völlig unterschiedliche Bewertungslogiken – weil die eine Immobilie ein Ort zum Leben ist und die andere eine Maschine, die Bargeld produziert.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization are three independent routes to one number, and the appraiser weights them rather than averaging them.
segments.tr: 1. Sachwert, Vergleichswert und Ertragswert sind drei unabhängige Wege zu einer Zahl, und der Gutachter gewichtet sie, anstatt sie zu mitteln.

segments.src: 2. Sales comparison rules owner-occupied housing; income capitalization rules investment property; cost approach covers new construction, insurance, and special-purpose buildings with no market to compare against.
segments.tr: 2. Das Vergleichswertverfahren dominiert bei selbstgenutztem Wohnraum; das Ertragswertverfahren dominiert bei Anlageimmobilien; das Sachwertverfahren deckt Neubauten, Versicherungen und Spezialgebäude ab, für die es keinen Vergleichsmarkt gibt.

segments.src: 3. `Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` is the whole income approach in one line — and NOI is always calculated before your mortgage payment.
segments.tr: 3. `Wert = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` ist der gesamte Ertragswertansatz in einer Zeile – und das NOI wird immer vor Ihrer Hypothekenzahlung berechnet.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **1.** A city is appraising a newly built public library.
segments.tr: **1.** Eine Stadt bewertet eine neu gebaute öffentliche Bibliothek.

segments.src: There are no comparable sales and it generates no rent.
segments.tr: Es gibt keine vergleichbaren Verkäufe und sie generiert keine Miete.

segments.src: Which approach carries the most weight?
segments.tr: Welcher Ansatz hat das größte Gewicht?

segments.src: - (A) Sales comparison
segments.tr: - (A) Vergleichswertverfahren

segments.src: - (B) Cost
segments.tr: - (B) Sachwertverfahren

segments.src: - (C) Income capitalization
segments.tr: - (C) Ertragswertverfahren

segments.src: - (D) Gross rent multiplier
segments.tr: - (D) Bruttomietmultiplikator

segments.src: **2.** A small retail strip produces $60,000 in NOI.
segments.tr: **2.** Ein kleiner Einzelhandelsstreifen erwirtschaftet $60.000 NOI.

segments.src: Comparable properties are trading at a 5% cap rate.
segments.tr: Vergleichbare Immobilien werden mit einer 5 % Cap Rate gehandelt.

segments.src: Estimated value?
segments.tr: Geschätzter Wert?

segments.src: **3.** (O/X) Your monthly mortgage payment is an operating expense and should be subtracted when calculating a property's NOI.
segments.tr: **3.** (R/F) Ihre monatliche Hypothekenzahlung ist eine Betriebskostenart und sollte bei der Berechnung des NOI einer Immobilie abgezogen werden.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Die heutigen Begriffe

segments.src: - **Comparable ("comp")** — A recently sold, genuinely similar property used as evidence of the subject's value.
segments.tr: - **Vergleichsobjekt ("Comp")** – Eine kürzlich verkaufte, wirklich ähnliche Immobilie, die als Nachweis für den Wert des Bewertungsobjekts dient.

segments.src: - **Accrued depreciation** — Total loss in value from all causes since construction: physical, functional, and external.
segments.tr: - **Kumulierte Abschreibung** – Gesamter Wertverlust aus allen Ursachen seit dem Bau: physisch, funktional und extern.

segments.src: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** — Income after vacancy and operating expenses, but *before* debt service and income taxes.
segments.tr: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** – Einkommen nach Leerstand und Betriebskosten, aber *vor* Schuldendienst und Einkommenssteuern.

segments.src: - **Capitalization rate** — The market-derived return investors demand, expressed as NOI divided by price.
segments.tr: - **Kapitalisierungssatz (Cap Rate)** – Die vom Markt abgeleitete Rendite, die Investoren verlangen, ausgedrückt als NOI geteilt durch den Preis.

segments.src: - **Reconciliation** — The appraiser's final judgment weighting the approaches into a single opinion of value.
segments.tr: - **Abstimmung (Reconciliation)** – Das abschließende Urteil des Gutachters, das die Ansätze zu einer einzigen Wertmeinung gewichtet.

segments.src: - **Appraisal gap** — The shortfall when a property appraises below the contract price, which the buyer must cover in cash.
segments.tr: - **Bewertungslücke (Appraisal Gap)** – Der Fehlbetrag, wenn eine Immobilie unter dem Vertragspreis bewertet wird, den der Käufer in bar decken muss.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B) Cost.** No comps and no income stream leaves only reconstruction cost less depreciation; this is the textbook special-purpose case.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **1 — (B) Sachwert.** Keine Vergleichswerte und kein Einkommensstrom lassen nur die Wiederaufbaukosten abzüglich Abschreibung übrig; dies ist der Lehrbuchfall für Spezialimmobilien.

segments.src: Note the leverage in that denominator: if the cap rate moved to 6%, the same income would be worth $1,000,000.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie die Hebelwirkung im Nenner: Wenn die Cap Rate auf 6 % steigen würde, wäre dasselbe Einkommen $1.000.000 wert.

segments.src: **3 — X (False).** Debt service is excluded from NOI.
segments.tr: **3 — F (Falsch).** Der Schuldendienst ist vom NOI ausgeschlossen.

segments.src: NOI measures what the property earns; your loan terms describe how you bought it, and two buyers with different mortgages would otherwise arrive at different "values" for the identical building.*
segments.tr: Das NOI misst, was die Immobilie verdient; Ihre Kreditbedingungen beschreiben, wie Sie sie gekauft haben, und zwei Käufer mit unterschiedlichen Hypotheken würden sonst zu unterschiedlichen „Werten“ für dasselbe Gebäude kommen.*

vi.title: [Bất động sản 101 #10] Ba cách để trả lời một câu hỏi: "Nơi này thực sự đáng giá bao nhiêu?"

segments.src: > An appraiser doesn't guess at a number — they triangulate it three ways: what it would cost to rebuild, what similar properties just sold for, and how much income it throws off.
segments.tr: > Một thẩm định viên không đoán mò một con số — họ xác định nó theo ba cách: chi phí để xây dựng lại, giá bán gần đây của các bất động sản tương tự, và thu nhập mà nó tạo ra.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: A price is what one buyer paid.
segments.tr: Giá cả là số tiền mà một người mua đã trả.

segments.src: **Value** is what a typical, informed buyer *would* pay — and that's a harder question, because every parcel of land on earth is unique.
segments.tr: **Giá trị** là số tiền mà một người mua thông thái, điển hình *sẽ* trả — và đó là một câu hỏi khó hơn, vì mọi mảnh đất trên trái đất đều là duy nhất.

segments.src: You can't look up "3-bed ranch in Raleigh" on a stock ticker.
segments.tr: Bạn không thể tra cứu "nhà 3 phòng ngủ ở Raleigh" trên bảng tin chứng khoán.

segments.src: So the appraisal profession settled on three independent routes to the same answer.
segments.tr: Vì vậy, nghề thẩm định đã thống nhất ba con đường độc lập để đi đến cùng một câu trả lời.

segments.src: Each one is a different question in disguise.
segments.tr: Mỗi con đường là một câu hỏi khác nhau được ngụy trang.

segments.src: The Cost Approach — "What would it cost to build this from scratch?"**
segments.tr: Phương pháp chi phí — "Sẽ tốn bao nhiêu để xây dựng cái này từ đầu?"**

segments.src: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value
segments.tr: Land value + cost to rebuild the improvements - accrued depreciation = value

segments.src: You value the land as if vacant, add what it would cost today to build an equivalent structure (*replacement cost*), then subtract everything that has eaten away at that new-building value.
segments.tr: Bạn định giá mảnh đất như thể nó đang trống, cộng với chi phí xây dựng một cấu trúc tương đương hiện nay (*chi phí thay thế*), sau đó trừ đi mọi thứ đã làm giảm giá trị của tòa nhà mới đó.

segments.src: That last part, **accrued depreciation**, comes in three flavors:
segments.tr: Phần cuối cùng đó, **khấu hao lũy kế**, có ba dạng:

segments.src: - *Physical deterioration* — the roof is 22 years old, the deck is soft.
segments.tr: - *Hao mòn vật lý* — mái nhà đã 22 năm tuổi, sàn gỗ bị mục.

segments.src: - *Functional obsolescence* — a 4-bedroom house with one bathroom, or a 9-foot ceiling in a warehouse district that now wants 32 feet.
segments.tr: - *Lỗi thời chức năng* — một ngôi nhà 4 phòng ngủ chỉ có một phòng tắm, hoặc trần nhà cao 9 feet trong một khu nhà kho hiện nay đòi hỏi trần cao 32 feet.

segments.src: - *External obsolescence* — nothing is wrong with the building; they just approved a highway interchange 300 feet away. This one is off-site, so the owner can't fix it at any price.
segments.tr: - *Lỗi thời ngoại cảnh* — không có gì sai với tòa nhà; chỉ là họ vừa phê duyệt một nút giao đường cao tốc cách đó 300 feet. Cái này nằm ngoài khuôn viên, nên chủ sở hữu không thể sửa chữa dù với bất kỳ giá nào.

segments.src: The cost approach is strongest for brand-new construction (little depreciation to estimate) and for **special-purpose property** — a church, a fire station, a municipal water treatment plant.
segments.tr: Phương pháp chi phí hiệu quả nhất đối với các công trình xây mới (ít khấu hao để ước tính) và đối với **bất động sản mục đích đặc biệt** — nhà thờ, trạm cứu hỏa, nhà máy xử lý nước thải đô thị.

segments.src: Nobody has "comparable sales" of fire stations, and a fire station doesn't collect rent.
segments.tr: Không ai có "giao dịch so sánh" cho các trạm cứu hỏa, và một trạm cứu hỏa không thu tiền thuê.

segments.src: It's also the approach behind your homeowner's insurance replacement coverage.
segments.tr: Đây cũng là phương pháp đằng sau bảo hiểm thay thế cho chủ nhà của bạn.

segments.src: The Sales Comparison Approach — "What did the neighbors get?"**
segments.tr: Phương pháp so sánh bán hàng — "Những người hàng xóm đã bán được bao nhiêu?"**

segments.src: Find three to five recent sales of genuinely similar properties (**comps**), then adjust *the comps* toward the subject property.
segments.tr: Tìm ba đến năm giao dịch gần đây của các bất động sản thực sự tương tự (**tài sản so sánh**), sau đó điều chỉnh *các tài sản so sánh* về phía bất động sản mục tiêu.

segments.src: Note the direction, because it trips everyone up: if the comp is **better** than your subject (it has the finished basement, yours doesn't), you **subtract** from the comp's sale price.
segments.tr: Lưu ý hướng điều chỉnh, vì nó khiến mọi người nhầm lẫn: nếu tài sản so sánh **tốt hơn** tài sản mục tiêu của bạn (nó có tầng hầm hoàn thiện, của bạn thì không), bạn **trừ** vào giá bán của tài sản so sánh đó.

segments.src: If the comp is worse, you add.
segments.tr: Nếu tài sản so sánh tệ hơn, bạn cộng vào.

segments.src: You never adjust the subject — the subject is the unknown you're solving for.
segments.tr: Bạn không bao giờ điều chỉnh tài sản mục tiêu — tài sản mục tiêu là ẩn số bạn đang cần giải.

segments.src: This is the dominant approach for houses, condos, and vacant land, and it's what a lender's appraisal on a single-family purchase leans on almost entirely.
segments.tr: Đây là phương pháp thống trị đối với nhà ở, căn hộ và đất trống, và là phương pháp mà thẩm định của bên cho vay đối với việc mua nhà đơn lập dựa vào gần như hoàn toàn.

segments.src: Its weakness is its dependency: it needs an active market of recent, arm's-length sales.
segments.tr: Điểm yếu của nó là sự phụ thuộc: nó cần một thị trường hoạt động tích cực với các giao dịch gần đây, minh bạch.

segments.src: In a thin rural market or a frozen one, there's nothing to compare against.
segments.tr: Ở một thị trường nông thôn thưa thớt hoặc thị trường đóng băng, không có gì để so sánh.

segments.src: The Income Capitalization Approach — "What does this thing earn?"**
segments.tr: Phương pháp vốn hóa thu nhập — "Thứ này kiếm được bao nhiêu?"**

segments.src: For property bought as an investment, value is a function of the income stream.
segments.tr: Đối với bất động sản được mua như một khoản đầu tư, giá trị là một hàm số của dòng thu nhập.

segments.src: The simplest form is **direct capitalization**:
segments.tr: Hình thức đơn giản nhất là **vốn hóa trực tiếp**:

segments.src: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate
segments.tr: Value = Net Operating Income (NOI) ÷ Capitalization Rate

segments.src: **NOI** is annual rent minus vacancy and collection loss, minus operating expenses (taxes, insurance, management, maintenance).
segments.tr: **NOI** là tiền thuê hàng năm trừ đi tỷ lệ trống và tổn thất thu nợ, trừ đi chi phí vận hành (thuế, bảo hiểm, quản lý, bảo trì).

segments.src: Critically, NOI is calculated *before* the mortgage.
segments.tr: Quan trọng là, NOI được tính *trước* khi trả nợ vay thế chấp.

segments.src: Debt service is not an operating expense — it describes how *you* financed the deal, not what the building earns.
segments.tr: Dịch vụ nợ không phải là chi phí vận hành — nó mô tả cách *bạn* tài trợ cho thương vụ, không phải tòa nhà kiếm được bao nhiêu.

segments.src: Two buyers with different loans face the same NOI.
segments.tr: Hai người mua với các khoản vay khác nhau vẫn đối mặt với cùng một NOI.

segments.src: The **cap rate** is the market's required return, pulled from what comparable investment properties recently sold for.
segments.tr: **Tỷ lệ vốn hóa (cap rate)** là lợi nhuận yêu cầu của thị trường, được rút ra từ giá bán gần đây của các bất động sản đầu tư tương tự.

segments.src: Lower cap rate = higher price per dollar of income = investors see it as safer or expect growth.
segments.tr: Tỷ lệ vốn hóa thấp hơn = giá cao hơn trên mỗi đô la thu nhập = các nhà đầu tư coi nó an toàn hơn hoặc kỳ vọng tăng trưởng.

segments.src: For longer, lumpier income streams — a 12-year office lease with step-ups — appraisers use *yield capitalization*, discounting projected future cash flows back to present value (a DCF).
segments.tr: Đối với các dòng thu nhập dài hạn, không đều — ví dụ hợp đồng thuê văn phòng 12 năm với các bước tăng giá — các thẩm định viên sử dụng *vốn hóa lợi nhuận*, chiết khấu các dòng tiền dự kiến trong tương lai về giá trị hiện tại (DCF).

segments.src: **Then comes reconciliation.** The appraiser develops whichever approaches are applicable and then **weights** them.
segments.tr: **Sau đó là bước đối chiếu.** Thẩm định viên phát triển bất kỳ phương pháp nào áp dụng được và sau đó **trọng số** chúng.

segments.src: This is not an average.
segments.tr: Đây không phải là một mức trung bình.

segments.src: For a suburban house, sales comparison carries nearly all the weight.
segments.tr: Đối với một ngôi nhà ngoại ô, phương pháp so sánh bán hàng chiếm gần như toàn bộ trọng số.

segments.src: For a new distribution center leased to a national tenant, income leads.
segments.tr: Đối với một trung tâm phân phối mới cho thuê cho một khách thuê quốc gia, thu nhập chiếm ưu thế.

segments.src: For that fire station, cost is basically all you have.
segments.tr: Đối với trạm cứu hỏa đó, chi phí về cơ bản là tất cả những gì bạn có.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong cuộc sống hàng ngày

segments.src: You're under contract on a house outside Charlotte, NC at **$420,000**.
segments.tr: Bạn đang ký hợp đồng mua một ngôi nhà bên ngoài Charlotte, NC với giá **$420,000**.

segments.src: You're putting 20% down and financing the rest.
segments.tr: Bạn trả trước 20% và vay phần còn lại.

segments.src: Two weeks in, the lender's appraisal comes back at **$405,000**.
segments.tr: Hai tuần sau, thẩm định của bên cho vay trả về con số **$405,000**.

segments.src: Here's why that stings.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao điều đó gây đau đớn.

segments.src: A lender lends against the **lesser** of the purchase price or the appraised value.
segments.tr: Bên cho vay dựa trên giá trị **thấp hơn** giữa giá mua hoặc giá trị thẩm định.

segments.src: At $420,000 you'd borrow $336,000 and bring $84,000.
segments.tr: Ở mức $420,000, bạn sẽ vay $336,000 và bỏ ra $84,000.

segments.src: At an appraised $405,000 the loan caps at $324,000 — so if the seller won't budge on price, you now need **$96,000** in cash.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization are three independent routes to one number, and the appraiser weights them rather than averaging them.
segments.tr: 1. Chi phí, so sánh bán hàng và vốn hóa thu nhập là ba con đường độc lập dẫn đến một con số, và thẩm định viên tính trọng số cho chúng thay vì lấy trung bình.

segments.src: 2. Sales comparison rules owner-occupied housing; income capitalization rules investment property; cost approach covers new construction, insurance, and special-purpose buildings with no market to compare against.
segments.tr: 2. So sánh bán hàng thống trị nhà ở chủ sở hữu sử dụng; vốn hóa thu nhập thống trị bất động sản đầu tư; phương pháp chi phí bao phủ xây dựng mới, bảo hiểm và các tòa nhà mục đích đặc biệt không có thị trường để so sánh.

segments.src: 3. `Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate` is the whole income approach in one line — and NOI is always calculated before your mortgage payment.
segments.tr: 3. `Giá trị = NOI ÷ Tỷ lệ vốn hóa` là toàn bộ phương pháp thu nhập trong một dòng — và NOI luôn được tính trước khi trả nợ vay thế chấp.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Comparable ("comp")** — A recently sold, genuinely similar property used as evidence of the subject's value.
segments.tr: - **Tài sản so sánh ("comp")** — Một bất động sản tương tự, được bán gần đây, dùng làm bằng chứng cho giá trị của tài sản mục tiêu.

segments.src: - **Accrued depreciation** — Total loss in value from all causes since construction: physical, functional, and external.
segments.tr: - **Khấu hao lũy kế** — Tổng giá trị bị mất từ mọi nguyên nhân kể từ khi xây dựng: vật lý, chức năng và ngoại cảnh.

segments.src: - **Net Operating Income (NOI)** — Income after vacancy and operating expenses, but *before* debt service and income taxes.
segments.tr: - **Thu nhập hoạt động ròng (NOI)** — Thu nhập sau khi trừ tỷ lệ trống và chi phí vận hành, nhưng *trước* khi trả nợ và thuế thu nhập.

segments.src: - **Capitalization rate** — The market-derived return investors demand, expressed as NOI divided by price.
segments.tr: - **Tỷ lệ vốn hóa** — Lợi nhuận từ thị trường mà các nhà đầu tư yêu cầu, được biểu thị bằng NOI chia cho giá.

segments.src: - **Reconciliation** — The appraiser's final judgment weighting the approaches into a single opinion of value.
segments.tr: - **Đối chiếu** — Phán quyết cuối cùng của thẩm định viên khi tính trọng số các phương pháp thành một ý kiến giá trị duy nhất.

segments.src: - **Appraisal gap** — The shortfall when a property appraises below the contract price, which the buyer must cover in cash.
segments.tr: - **Khoảng cách thẩm định** — Sự thiếu hụt khi bất động sản được thẩm định thấp hơn giá hợp đồng, mà người mua phải bù bằng tiền mặt.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B) Cost.** No comps and no income stream leaves only reconstruction cost less depreciation; this is the textbook special-purpose case.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: **1 — (B) Chi phí.** Không có tài sản so sánh và không có dòng thu nhập chỉ để lại chi phí xây dựng lại trừ khấu hao; đây là trường hợp mục đích đặc biệt điển hình trong sách giáo khoa.

segments.src: Note the leverage in that denominator: if the cap rate moved to 6%, the same income would be worth $1,000,000.
segments.tr: Lưu ý đòn bẩy ở mẫu số đó: nếu tỷ lệ vốn hóa tăng lên 6%, cùng một mức thu nhập sẽ chỉ đáng giá $1,000,000.

segments.tr: **3 — X (Sai).** Dịch vụ nợ được loại trừ khỏi NOI.

segments.src: NOI measures what the property earns; your loan terms describe how you bought it, and two buyers with different mortgages would otherwise arrive at different "values" for the identical building.*
segments.tr: NOI đo lường những gì bất động sản kiếm được; các điều khoản khoản vay của bạn mô tả cách bạn mua nó, và hai người mua với các khoản vay khác nhau sẽ không thể đưa ra các "giá trị" khác nhau cho cùng một tòa nhà.*
